thesis: Sandisk has genuine cash strength and actual debt repayment to zero, but the bear carries the through-cycle valuation objection. A 3.60% adjusted annual FCF yield is much less forgiving than 6.30x forecast earnings when two-thirds of sequential revenue growth came from pricing and adjusted operating margin reached 79.20%. That imbalance supports waiting for a more durable cash basis without claiming an imminent NAND downturn or rejecting the verified cash normalization.
strongest_counterexample: $8.743bn adjusted annual FCF survives $2.476bn prepayment and $0.275bn venture-investment deductions; zero stated debt and $4.762bn cash can finance customer growth through softer pricing and make present earnings more durable than the bear assumes.
invalidation_conditions: Comparable adjusted annual FCF above $8.743bn after the same prepayment/venture deductions, while sequential pricing contribution falls below the disclosed two-thirds share, would weaken the peak-sensitive valuation ruling.
Adjusted annual FCF at or below zero with stated debt returning above zero would invalidate the current resilience counterweight.
decisive_factors: Normalization addresses cash exaggeration but does not establish through-cycle repeatability.
Deposits/commitments qualify available cash; technical history contains only 413 bars and cannot establish long historical comparability.
